transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (NovaFin Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Infra Lead), Sana Li (Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review the latest benchmark run vs the baseline provider (NovaFin's current vendor) — focusing on p95 latency, sustained throughput, and cost per token at production traffic mix. Discussed tuning done (batching, kv/prefix cache), outstanding infra constraints on customer side, and next steps (raw logs, SOC2, latency deep dive).

Topics covered:
- Baseline numbers and how Redwood compares (latency/throughput/cost)
- Tuning knobs we applied this week (dynamic batching, 4-bit quantization test, prefix cache)
- Observed regressions on long-context requests
- Security/compliance asks and SOC2 docs
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give a quick run through of the benchmark numbers then tunings we tried this week and then, um, open floor for Qs. Maya, Ethan, you good?
[00:12] Maya Patel: yeah all good thanks. hope you're doing well.
[00:15] Priya Rao: hey team, quick note i ran three separate runs — baseline reproduction, redwood hosted default, and redwood with caching+batching.
[00:22] Ethan Brooks: just to (mumble) confirm, the baseline provider is what we're currently running in prod, right ? bedrock-ish?
[00:27] Maya Patel: yeah it's their, uh, managed bedrock setup via AWS partner.
[00:31] Alex Chen: ok cool. so high level numbers — p95 latency at our 60% traffic mix: baseline p95 ~ 420ms, Redwood hosted default ~ 380ms, Redwood tuned (batching + prefix cache) ~ 260ms. throughput steady-state (tokens/sec) baseline ~ 12k, redwood tuned ~ 18k. cost per 1M tokens effective after batching: baseline =~ $44, redwood tuned =~ $29. these are approximate, see sheet.
[00:58] Maya Patel: interesting the p95 improvement is quite good — is that with the same model? we were using the open-llm-2 small for baseline and you used the, um, rdx-1-small?
[01:09] Priya Rao: good call — we matched architecture as closely as we could, both are llama-derivative 7B-ish. slight differences in tokenization and kernel implementations so raw numbers have noise, but the delta persists after normalizing for prompt mix.
[01:24] Ethan Brooks: where did the latency gain come from mostly? batching? kv cache? quant?
[01:28] Priya Rao: it's a mix. primary is continuous batching improvements — smarter packer reduced scheduling overhead by ~25% at our qps. second is prefix/KV caching for repetitive prompt prefixes — saved about 120ms on our test set. third is kernel selection: runtime picked an int4-friendly kernel path; we saw 5-8% improvement.
[01:46] Maya Patel: ok, but we did see a regression on long-context requests in the tuned run? any explanation?
[01:52] Priya Rao: yes — good catch. for sequences > 1k tokens the quantized path introduced slightly more decode variance: p99 spikes up. we suspect cache invalidation frequency + KV eviction policy interacting with our test harness. we rolled a fix candidate today to change the eviction window and re-run.
[02:10] Alex Chen: to be explicit: p95 better but p99 for big contexts can be worse if you push quant aggressively. for your workloads we need to pick the quant/profile that's a win for your 95/99 goals.
[02:21] Sana Li: on security side, quick Q — raw logs include inputs? how do we redact? and SOC2?
[02:27] Jordan Kim: good q. Jordan here — for the POC we can provide redacted logs, and we have a SOC2 summary and mini-AICPA pack we can share. full SOC2 report needs an NDA but summary and controls mapping is fine. i'll share the doc after call.
[02:42] Maya Patel: perfect. also can you share the exact test harness config? seed, prompt set etc?
[02:47] Priya Rao: yes — i'll push the harness config and the raw run logs to the shared drive. note there is some noise from tokenization differences so we'll include the tokenization reconciliation file.
[02:59] Ethan Brooks: on infra limits — i noticed during the run you pegged one GPU at times and fallback happened to smaller instance; can you explain autoscaling behavior?
[03:07] Priya Rao: we used a tiny dedicated pool in the sandbox to simulate constrained infra. autoscaling in hosted triggers after sustained queue depth — for the POC we kept upper bound low to emulate your capacity plan. the pegging you saw was intentional to measure tail latency under stress.
[03:20] Ethan Brooks: ok thanks. what's the difference if we go dedicated? do numbers change?
[03:24] Alex Chen: dedicated will reduce variance — lower multi-tenant noise and more predictable p99. our Dedicated runs for similar config show p95~240ms and p99~560ms for long-context with tuned caching. cost goes up but unit cost per token often drops for sustained traffic due to reserved capacity.
[03:39] Maya Patel: are there any stability concerns with prefix caching? we rely on strong determinism for audits.
[03:44] Priya Rao: prefix caching is deterministic functionally, but eviction timing can influence observed latency; for audit determinism we can provide cache logs and deterministic replay to prove identical outputs.
[03:54] Alex Chen: also worth noting we have an option to pin model versions and kernel profiles so you get identical behavior across runs.
[04:01] Maya Patel: ok. on the cost numbers, you said $29 vs $44 per million tokens — is that with batch credit applied? how sensitive is that to burstiness?
[04:09] Priya Rao: yes numbers include batching efficiency at your 60% mix. if traffic becomes more spiky (bursty) batching gains drop and cost approaches baseline. we estimated at 90% burstiness the gap narrows to ~$6-8 per million.
[04:23] Ethan Brooks: do you support on-prem or VPC private deploys? our compliance team prefer private control plane ideally.
[04:29] Alex Chen: yes Redwood Private is exactly for that — VPC deployments with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations. the POC can pivot to a private pilot; timeline is longer (we'll need infra access and compliance kickoff).
[04:41] Sana Li: timeline and docs please — how long to get private pilot up?
[04:45] Jordan Kim: typical private pilot is 4-8 weeks depending on access and approvals. we'll send the onboarding checklist and required network rules.
[04:52] Maya Patel: great. any concerns about model drift/regression monitoring during the POC?
[04:57] Priya Rao: we enabled quality monitoring in the sandbox — we flagged two prompts with higher hallucination rates after quantization; we can run regression evals tied to your golden prompts and set alerts.
[05:07] Maya Patel: can you attach the list of flagged prompts?
[05:10] Priya Rao: yes, that'll be in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Alex Chen: ok summarizing next technical items: we'll push raw logs + harness (Alex), Priya will re-run p95 focused long-context test with eviction window tweak and share results, Jordan will share SOC2 summary + private pilot checklist. Maya to confirm prod traffic mix next week.
[05:28] Maya Patel: sounds good. quick pricing ask — can you provide a rough Dedicated estimate if we commit to 3-month reserved pool?
[05:34] Alex Chen: yes i'll put together a conservative estimate and breakout (reserved vs burst). won't be final but should be good enough for internal budgeting.
[05:41] Ethan Brooks: one last technical thing — do you support hybrid routing between hosted and dedicated for cost control? like low-latency requests go to dedicated, bulk offline to hosted?
[05:49] Priya Rao: yep, routing policies support latency, cost and region tiers. we can configure real-time routing based on headers or route tags.
[05:55] Maya Patel: excellent. thanks everyone.
[05:58] Alex Chen: thanks team. we'll follow up with artifacts by EOD tomorrow.
